prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1500; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim file for that.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic was light.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was going about twenty-five miles an hour and slowing down for a turn. The other car came over into my lane.

Q: Was there any warning before the contact?

A: Not really. I hit my brakes and turned a little, but there wasn't time to avoid it. It was a head-on hit, though not a hard one.

Q: Did either vehicle's airbags deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. Both cars drove off on their own, but my car had a lot of damage to the front end.

Q: How are you feeling since the accident?

A: My lower back is sore. It stiffened up overnight and I've had trouble bending and sitting for long periods. I went to urgent care the next day.

Q: Have you had any prior back problems?

A: I had some soreness years ago after lifting something heavy, but nothing that required treatment or time off work.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm following the doctor's instructions and I want to get back to normal as soon as possible.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Okay, thank you.
